passage.title: The School Science Project
passage.text: Anna is a student who loves science. She wants to become a scientist one day. Every Friday, her class does a small research project. This month, Anna has a theory. She thinks that bean plants grow better in natural sunlight than under a desk lamp. Her teacher likes the idea and asks the class to do an experiment. First, Anna chooses a simple method. She prepares two small plants. Both plants have the same soil and the same amount of water. The only difference is the light. One plant stays near the window, and the other stays under a lamp. Every afternoon, Anna measures the plants. She writes the data in her notebook. She also adds useful information, such as the weather and the room temperature. She is careful because good research needs correct data. After three weeks, Anna looks at all the results. The plant near the window is taller and has more green leaves. The evidence is clear. Her teacher says the experiment was successful. Anna is excited because she can discover something new. She understands that one experiment cannot prove every theory, but it helps people learn. The project gives her more knowledge about plants and shows her that science is interesting and useful.

passage.title: A Good Science Class
passage.text: Mr. Brown is a science teacher at Green Hill School. He wants his students to become more knowledgeable about the world. Every month, the class works on a small research project. The students enjoy learning by doing simple activities. This month, the class wants to discover which drink helps bean plants grow best. Before they begin, Mr. Brown explains the methodology of the project. He tells everyone to use the same method so the results will be fair. Each group prepares three plants with the same soil, the same pots, and the same amount of light. Each group has a different hypothesis. One group believes water is the best. Another group thinks milk will help the plants grow faster. A third group chooses a plant drink. Then the students start the experiment. Every afternoon, they measure the plants and record the data. They also write useful information in their notebooks. At the end of two weeks, they compare all the results. The evidence clearly shows that water helps the plants grow best. The milk and the plant drink do not improve growth. Mr. Brown explains that one experiment does not prove every theory. Good scientists repeat the test many times before they accept a conclusion. They also share their results with other researchers. When different people get the same results, the evidence becomes stronger. The students are happy with their project. They learn that science is not only about finding the right answer. It is also about asking good questions, using the correct method, collecting accurate data, and learning from every discovery. The project gives them more knowledge and makes them more interested in science.

passage.title: Science and Research
passage.transcript: Good morning, everyone. Today we are going to learn about science and research. Every scientist does research to learn new things and build more knowledge. Before starting an experiment, the scientist has a clear theory. Then, he or she chooses the best method to test the idea. A good method helps make the experiment fair and accurate. During the experiment, the scientist collects data every day. The data may include numbers, pictures, or simple notes. The scientist also writes important information in a notebook. Good information helps people understand the results better. After the experiment, the scientist studies all the data carefully. Sometimes the evidence is strong, but sometimes more research is needed. If the evidence is clear, the scientist may discover something new. This discovery can help people solve problems or improve their lives. Science is very important because it helps us understand the world. Every experiment, every piece of evidence, and every new discovery gives us more knowledge. By doing careful research and using the right method, scientists continue to make our future better.
